brief.situation: You are the developer on call for recs-api, the recommendations API of Fernhill Books (fictional), running on Azure Container Apps in single revision mode. Release v42 moves the database password from a plain Container Apps secret to a Key Vault reference, so that the rotation security runs at 10:45 is picked up automatically. At 10:00 the pipeline reports that revision v42 never became ready; v41 still serves all traffic with the old password, which stops working at 10:45. Find out why v42 fails, get a working revision serving before 10:45, and do it without widening anyone's access.
handover: recs-api has a system-assigned managed identity. kv-recs uses Azure RBAC, not access policies.
You may create role assignments on resources in rg-recs.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments come from its list.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The incident keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, service or job and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident record: how you found why v42 never became ready, what you changed and why that scope, and what makes the next Key Vault reference work first time.

parts.label: Diagnosis
parts.criteria: Uses the revision state and the system logs (not the empty console logs) to find the 403 on the Key Vault reference, then confirms the managed identity has no role on the vault.
parts.modelAnswer: revision list showed v42 Failed with v41 still at 100%; the system log showed SecretRefFailed, 403 from kv-recs; role assignment list for the app's principal ID was empty.

parts.label: Least-privilege fix
parts.criteria: Grants Key Vault Secrets User to the app's identity at the vault scope, makes a new revision and lets single revision mode switch traffic when it is ready; rejects Key Vault Administrator at subscription scope, a pasted plain secret (which misses the rotation) and forcing traffic to a failed revision.
parts.modelAnswer: I assigned Key Vault Secrets User on kv-recs only and created revision v42b; once it passed its probes, traffic moved from v41 automatically. Administrator on the subscription would let the app manage every vault; a plain secret would break at 10:45; forcing traffic to v42 would have taken the API down.

parts.label: Prevention
parts.criteria: Ships the role assignment with the Key Vault reference in infrastructure as code, scoped to the vault.
parts.modelAnswer: The Bicep for recs-api now creates the identity's Key Vault Secrets User assignment on kv-recs next to the secret reference.

scoring.modelReasoning: v42 failed to provision and single revision mode left v41 serving. No container started, so console logs are empty; the system log shows SecretRefFailed with 403 from kv-recs. The app's managed identity has no role on the vault. Grant Key Vault Secrets User at the vault scope, create a new revision and let it take traffic once ready; then the versionless reference follows the 10:45 rotation. Key Vault Administrator on the subscription is far too broad, a pasted plain secret breaks at 10:45, and forcing traffic to the failed revision causes the outage you are trying to avoid.
